papers.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
papers.problem: Live game commentary models know when to speak but not what the new game's objects are.
papers.fix: A wiki-reading helper agent raised object recall from 0.082 to 0.116 and cut leakage from 9.9% to 1.0%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Pair a small live model with a lookup agent, so it can name unseen things without retraining.
papers.limitation: Tests used one training game and ten unseen games, so other setups may differ.

papers.title: History Forcing: Distilling History-Dependent Continuations for Long-Horizon Video World Models
papers.problem: Fast AI video generators lose track of scenes and objects after the camera looks away.
papers.fix: History Forcing raised object consistency from 58.43 to 62.18 on MemoBench and scene quality from 2.35 to 2.70.
papers.practicalUseCase: Expect fewer broken scenes in long generated videos, so favor models trained with history in mind.

papers.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
papers.problem: Nobody knew how well AI models pick research directions and plans compared with human researchers.
papers.fix: AI proposals reached only 26% of human level on citations and 18% on ideas, across 90,000 proposals.
papers.practicalUseCase: Treat AI as a weak research planner, so use it to explore directions and keep concrete plans human.
papers.limitation: The benchmark compares AI proposals against 2026 papers from four research areas.

papers.title: Order-Only On-Policy Distillation
papers.problem: Small models copy a big model's token confidence poorly, and results shift with the teacher temperature setting.
papers.fix: Copying only the teacher's token ranking beat the usual method in all six teacher-student pairs, by up to 2.9 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: Train small models on rankings alone, so you can skip temperature tuning.
papers.limitation: Tests covered math benchmarks only: HMMT25, AIME24, and AIME25.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks create sustainability committees, but nobody knew if they change environmental results at Islamic banks.
papers.fix: Committees raised environmental scores in all banks, but at Islamic banks they mainly lifted overall and resource-reduction scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: Judge an Islamic bank by its green products, not its committee, because the committee may be symbolic.
papers.limitation: Panel regressions in emerging markets show links, not cause.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Few people knew what drives the size of sustainability sukuk issues.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts and USD or Euro denomination led to larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger sustainability sukuk should use equity-based contracts, and should weigh second party opinion costs.
papers.limitation: The data ends in 2022, and sustainability sukuk remain a tiny share of the market.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan did not know if AI and big data improve their results.
papers.fix: AI use, big data skills, and data management all link positively to competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.practicalUseCase: Invest in AI and data systems, and do not rely on staff digital skills alone.
papers.limitation: The survey covers 214 managers at 15 Jordanian banks at one point in time.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in dual systems did not know which digital and national factors drive their growth.
papers.fix: ICT adoption drove bank growth most, across 218 Islamic and conventional banks in 12 countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital investment pays off for both bank types, so back digital infrastructure before other growth levers.
papers.limitation: High-tech exports alone had no significant effect, and the data covers only 12 countries.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many people in Muslim-majority countries stay outside formal finance, even as Islamic finance grows.
papers.fix: In OIC countries, income, education, institutions, and internet access drive financial inclusion, unlike in OECD countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries should fund digital infrastructure and empower youth and women, so more people join formal finance.
papers.limitation: The study uses 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD
papers.problem: Little data showed how early-career academics with ADHD experience building a career.
papers.fix: Academia can reward ADHD traits, but social and institutional pressure often blocks that benefit.
papers.practicalUseCase: Pick workplaces that fit how you work, because the environment decides whether ADHD helps or hurts.
papers.limitation: This is an interview study, so it gives rich accounts but no measured effect size.

papers.title: Procrastination among US college students: Prevalence and impact relative to common health and life issues
papers.problem: People did not know how common procrastination is for students compared with other life issues.
papers.fix: Procrastination affected 72.3% of 65,950 US students, and harmed grades for 45.4% of them.
papers.practicalUseCase: Procrastination hurts grades far more than most issues, so fix it before chasing smaller problems.
papers.limitation: Self-reported US college data shows links, not cause.
